methodological_rigor.justification: Open-label, multicenter, parallel-cohort, randomized phase II study (NCT04919512, SunRISe-4) with 5:3 randomization stratified by TURBT completeness and T stage. Primary endpoint pCR is rigorously assessed by central blinded histopathology, with 94% local-central concordance. Sensitivity analyses include full analysis set and efficacy-evaluable set, with subgroup analyses across tumor stage and residual disease. IDMC-monitored, ICH-GCP compliant. Clopper-Pearson 95% CIs and Kaplan-Meier for RFS are appropriate. Biomarker analyses are prespecified exploratory and use Fisher's exact test and log-rank tests. Key limitation: side-by-side descriptive comparison with no formal between-cohort hypothesis test (authors acknowledge), and short follow-up (median 14.1 months).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual randomized phase II trial (Oxford 1b) addressing an unmet need: neoadjuvant therapy for cisplatin-ineligible or cisplatin-refusing MIBC patients. pCR of 37.5% with TAR-200+cetrelimab matches NIAGARA GC+durvalumab (37%) and substantially exceeds RC-alone historical 12-15%. First demonstration of combined local sustained gemcitabine delivery plus systemic checkpoint inhibition in MIBC, with manageable safety and no surgery delays. Has near-term practice-changing potential and supports bladder-sparing trial directions.

reporting_quality.justification: CONSORT diagram included (Fig 1); sponsor oversight, IDMC, ICH-GCP compliance, and written consent documented. Endpoints, stratification, treatment schedule (TAR-200 225mg q3w x4, cetrelimab 360mg IV q3w x4), surgical window (11-15 weeks), imaging schedule, and analysis populations are clearly defined. Biomarker assays are specifically identified (Natera Signatera for ctDNA, Convergent Genomics UROAmp for utDNA, Roche SP263 for PD-L1). However, the side-by-side descriptive-only comparison without between-cohort testing is an unusual CONSORT item, and additional statistical details (sample-size determination, prespecified thresholds) are relegated to the Data Supplement.

novelty_literature.justification: First study to demonstrate the contribution of sustained intravesical chemotherapy delivery (TAR-200) added to systemic checkpoint inhibition (cetrelimab) in the neoadjuvant MIBC setting. Largest study to date to explore utDNA as a biomarker in MIBC, with strong correlation of week-12 utDNA negativity with pCR (AUC 0.80, P<1e-5). Extends prior neoadjuvant ICI monotherapy and NAC-plus-ICI studies with a novel delivery mechanism; not a completely first-in-class biology but a distinctive therapeutic combination.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-structured IMRAD manuscript with clear endpoint definitions, three figures (CONSORT, Kaplan-Meier RFS, MRD biomarker panels with ROC) and three tables. Discussion is balanced, placing findings in context of NIAGARA and PURE-01/ABACUS/KEYNOTE. Concordance reporting between local and central pathology (94%) strengthens trust. Prose is clear; abstract accurately summarizes the primary and biomarker findings.

key_strengths: Randomized phase II (n=159) addressing cisplatin-ineligible/refusing MIBC with pCR 37.5% for TAR-200+cetrelimab vs 28.3% for cetrelimab alone
Central blinded pathology review with 94% local-central concordance
12-month RFS 77.4% (combination) vs 64.1% (monotherapy) providing early survival signal
Manageable safety: grade >=3 TRAE 15.8% combination vs 10.3% monotherapy; no treatment delays of RC beyond 8.2%
Robust exploratory biomarkers: utDNA negativity at week 12 strongly predicts pCR (AUC 0.80, P=5.4e-6); ctDNA status correlates with RFS (HR 4.42 baseline; 4.66 week 12)
key_concerns: Side-by-side descriptive-only design with no formal hypothesis test between cohorts limits definitive combination-benefit inference
Short follow-up (median 14.1 months); median RFS not reached in either cohort; overall survival not yet evaluable
Exclusion of residual tumors >3 cm limits generalizability to bulkier residual disease
Biomarker analyses are exploratory with small sample sizes (e.g., 30 utDNA-clearance evaluable patients)
Sponsor-designed and -analyzed trial with data transcribed into sponsor database; no independent data sharing described
chief_reviewer.rationale: A well-conducted randomized phase II with a novel intravesical-chemotherapy-plus-checkpoint combination, strong pCR results, and compelling biomarker findings; suitable for a top-tier oncology journal (Tier 1) with minor revisions.
